title: Counting Window for Prior Fines on a Parking License
content:
**Counting window for other fines** (Parking License violation fines). The span of months over which a license's other fines are counted depends on whether the license has recently been reinstated after a suspension and on how long it has been held.

**Definition.** When a reinstatement fee was billed on the license in the 24 months before the handling date, other fines are counted over a window of 24 months; when no reinstatement fee was billed in those months and the license has been held fewer than 365 days, other fines are counted over a window of 6 months; in every other case other fines are counted over a window of 12 months.

- A **reinstatement fee** line on the license is the record that privileges were restored after a suspension.
- **Days held** run from the license's start date to the handling date.
- Each window ends on the handling date and reaches back the stated number of months.

## Window by case

| Reinstatement fee billed on the license in the 24 months before the handling date | Days held | Counting window for other fines |
|---|---|---|
| yes | any | 24 months |
| no | fewer than 365 | 6 months |
| no | 365 or more | 12 months |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical licenses without a reinstatement fee in the last 24 months)

- Held 364 days: fewer than 365, so the window is 6 months.
- Held 365 days: not fewer than 365, so the window is 12 months.

A license held only 100 days that nevertheless carries a reinstatement fee in the last 24 months counts over 24 months: the reinstatement case is decided first.
